title: CORS issues with output: "export" due to unnecessary crossorigin attributes

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue was opened via the bug report template.

body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/tdanecker/export-crossorigin-issue

### To Reproduce

```bash
npm run build
```

inspect `./out/index.html`

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Generated link and script tags contain `crossorigin=""`, which is equivalent to `crossorigin="anonymous"`. This forces the browser to do CORS checks, even if the resources could be loaded with no-cors otherwise. See: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/crossorigin

Example from the generated index.html:
```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/_next/static/css/df8ddea784076f40.css" crossorigin="" data-precedence="next"/>
```


**Expected behavior:**

Link and script tags are generated without `crossorigin=""` attributes, as is the case when using other `output` modes.

Example:
```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/_next/static/css/df8ddea784076f40.css" data-precedence="next"/>
```

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
  Platform: linux
  Arch: x64
  Version: #40~22.04.1-Ubuntu SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Thu Nov 16 10:53:04 UTC 2
Binaries:
  Node: 20.11.0
  npm: 10.2.4
  Yarn: 3.6.1
  pnpm: 7.33.5
Relevant Packages:
  next: 14.1.0
  eslint-config-next: 14.1.0
  react: 18.2.0
  react-dom: 18.2.0
  typescript: 5.3.3
Next.js Config:
  output: export
```


### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Static HTML Export (output: "export")

next build (local), Vercel (Deployed), Other (Deployed)
